g-FS.st: Florence gold-quartz excitement, May 1881: May 1881: 'The gold excitement still seems to be on the increase' at Florence. Quartz ledges said to yield $750 a ton; Dr. Bond had a specimen; the best quartz came from near the Pine River by the granite to the south. The same item ran again in the Crystal Falls Diamond Drill in 1887.
src: Chronicling America, Watertown Republican, May 11, 1881, p. 1

t-rep-delhi.st: Add: in 1907 the Redwood Gazette recalled 'expensive undertakings made for gold along the Minnesota north of Delhi nearly twenty years ago,' with remains of buildings and stamping machinery still seen until recently. Capt. Jacob Hinderman of Ridgely township told the New Ulm News about the gold fever. In July 1894 over 500 people visited a mine where gold quartz came from a 12-foot hole (Redwood Gazette, Jul 19, 1894, p. 5; check that it is the same mine).
src: Chronicling America, Redwood Gazette, Aug 7, 1907, p. 1
